entry.title: Relays against an activity-matched control (13 Oct 2026, our own test, pre-registered, brain only): The two sides disagree: on one side silencing the relays lowered the turn neuron's rate more than matched activity elsewhere, on the other it did not. We do not draw a conclusion. Left eye: nothing silenced 21-25 Hz, matched control 13-34 Hz, relays E2 16.0 Hz, PVLP141 17.7 Hz; right eye 40-49, 40-43, 25.7, 27.0 Hz. 5 seeds and 5 matched draws per side, 3 relay seeds; some draws include direct inputs to the turn neuron; E2 is mostly PVLP141; not fly behaviour. The 9 Oct summary line stays with a dated note (its random control removed 2-6 times as much activity).

New plain answer (13 Oct 2026): Can a fly brain learn maths, to hack or to play a game? Our reading of what changes with practice in 13 projects, each claim attributed to its project; the 13 catalogue entries gain a learning field and a "What is learned" note.

140 catalogue entries (13 Oct 2026): 6 new: malecns-visual-motor (A), malecns-keratitis-pilot (A, a negative result), fly-chess (B), adfly-connectome (B), fly-brain-sim (B) and FlyGift (B, linked by its source repository only).

Controls ledger (13 Oct 2026): 53 studies, 44 with a wiring null: helps 21, no difference 10, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. Three rows joined from the authors' own numbers: malecns-visual-motor (helps), malecns-keratitis-pilot (no difference) and fly-brain-sim (helps, lab-notebook ranges).

Moved by their owner (13 Oct 2026): ChessFly and fly67 moved from github.com/znatgost to github.com/gexhaw (GitHub 301; the old demo pages answer 404). Try and source links now point to gexhaw; grades unchanged until the next re-check.

Verdict freshness (13 Oct 2026): the repositories of 14 of the 21 verdict rows re-checked, none with new code since grading; 56 of 56 videos available; fly64 and fly-terraria citations corrected; flydoom's repository still answers 404.
New report: Fifteenth check (13 Oct 2026), with the relay design, deviations, matched-draw details, the learning reading, new entries, tracking and limits.

Not decided: a second, lower-memory attempt on 12 Oct also needed more memory than our shared machine has (about 3 GB at its peak; the machine allows 3 GB for everything running on it). Measured: it ran out while preparing the moving-edge test input, before the first simulation step (sampled peak about 3.17 GB of the 3.22 GB limit). No result in either direction, no ledger row, no chart; the 10 Oct note is kept as dated history.

Re-check (12 Oct 2026): 10 graded entries (Bad Apple Fly, Stonkfly, Flyhard, DOOMFLY, Fly64, Fly Brain Minecraft, FlyBridge, Digital Fly in Terraria, Fly OCR, FlyLeno) re-read line by line at their graded commits; no new code and no grade change. Two texts fixed: Stonkfly's learning-rule description, and the DOOMFLY announcement video card (the clause about read-out cells "chosen because they responded to the screen" is not in the cited files).

Controls ledger (12 Oct 2026): 50 studies, 41 with a wiring null: helps 19, no difference 9, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. One row joined, from the authors' own numbers, scored only by our fixed rules: duth-x-stepmania: the authors compared the real wiring with 3 degree-preserving rewired copies (mean) on StepMania hit rate on the 152-note Edit chart. Real 0.9737, null 0.4013 (3 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as helps. Quality: fair, moderate; one seed; the readout groups are taken from the real wiring; 3 rewired copies.

Catalogue (12 Oct 2026): 134 entries, 2 new, each graded from code: duth-x-stepmania (A, ledger row helps) and flyonenomics (B, spiking activity only, no wiring control). Project claims are the projects' own.

Video gallery (12 Oct 2026): 56 videos, all available; 15 view counts refreshed from search pages, for example FlyLeno's playthrough video approximately 53,325 views on 12 Oct 2026. Catalogue record texts no longer carry their own view numbers; every count comes from videos.json with "approximately" and its date.
For AI agents (12 Oct 2026): release date, release id and counts first; the verdict count is now read from the verdict freshness data; flyvis guidance covers both attempts.
New report: fourteenth check (12 Oct 2026), with the flyvis steps and measurements, the 10-entry re-check, the new ledger row, admissions, triage, tracking and limits.

Controls ledger (11 Oct 2026): 49 studies, 40 with a wiring null: helps 18, no difference 9, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. Five rows joined, from the authors' own numbers, scored only by our fixed rules: fly-distill: the authors compared the real wiring with a degree-preserving shuffle on bits per byte (lower is better). Real 3.9572, null 3.9171 (4 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as mixed. flywire-connectome (the author's mushroom-body rate model): the authors compared the real wiring with strength-preserving null wirings (median of 100) on odour discrimination d'. Real 18.32, null 19.45 (100 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as worse. brainlab: the authors compared the real wiring with a target-permuted copy on held-out decision accuracy (%). Real 92.91, null 92.20 (1 null sample). Our ledger rules read this as no-difference. MelanoGraph: the authors compared the real wiring with a degree-preserving rewired copy on the receiver's gain over a resampled message. Real 0.4941, null 0 (1 null sample). Our ledger rules read this as helps. fly-arithmetic: the authors compared the real wiring with a random network of the same size on held-out addition accuracy (%). Real 48, null 98 (10 null samples). Our ledger rules read this as worse. Quality: fly-distill fair, strong; flywire-connectome partly fair, strong; brainlab partly fair, weak; MelanoGraph partly fair, weak; fly-arithmetic partly fair, strong.

Catalogue flag changes (11 Oct 2026): fly-distill no-difference to mixed; flywire-connectome-scz mixed to worse (task metric only); brainlab not-tested to no-difference (a task metric was found in its committed results; its trained_class is now whole-network-or-per-synapse).

Catalogue (11 Oct 2026): 132 entries, 4 new, each graded from code: MelanoGraph (A, ledger row helps), fly-arithmetic (A, ledger row worse), FlyRoyale (B, no results committed) and connectome-control-exploration (B, lesion and input controls only). Project claims are quoted from their READMEs.

Does it actually run? (11 Oct 2026): fly-arithmetic's website ran in our headless Chromium 154 without a GPU and with no action from us; first activity after about 11.2 s, about 2.05 MB; where it computes is unclear; we did not type a sum. 9 of 12 checked demos have run.

Video gallery (11 Oct 2026): 56 videos, all available; 18 view counts refreshed. Every view count on the site now comes from videos.json with "approximately" and its date, for example the dzuma "learns to hack" video approximately 70,445 views on 11 Oct 2026.
